comparison: Both evaluate SAXS data (C64-C67, C118). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with good χ² values, acknowledging 'flexible appendages' is an inference. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'scattering curves and envelopes look very similar' and recommend not making firm conclusions due to low resolution ambiguities.

Both evaluate COMMD-COMMD interaction data (C78-C86). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on systematic pull-down assays and domain mapping. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning data quality (Commd8 band identity) and noting interactions are 'quite promiscuous' with unclear principles for homo- vs heterodimer preference.

Both evaluate COMMD-CCDC interaction data (C90-C98). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with multiple complementary approaches including quantitative BLI. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing data quality concerns: minimal CCDC22 expression, apparent GST non-specific binding, and 'uninterpretable' results requiring improved experiments.

Both evaluate cross-linking mass spectrometry data (C99-C102). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and molecular-level detail. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED in second round, acknowledging results 'narrow down the potential interface,' though noting the WRVD motif is part of the dimerization core.

Both evaluate membrane binding data (C103-C112). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with qualitative and quantitative data plus mutagenesis validation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting lack of negative control (pure PC liposomes) and that the basic patch is not conserved in other membrane-binding family members.

Both evaluate cellular localization of membrane-binding mutant (C114-C116). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the result is surprising but highlights complexity of membrane recruitment. Peer reviewers accepted the findings without challenge, which helped address concerns about biological relevance.

Both evaluate structural homology analysis (C68-C77, C120). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with quantitative DALI metrics, noting functional implications remain speculative. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating comparisons 'do not contribute much' and are 'distractive,' with no support for functional similarities, recommending shortening or moving to supplement.

Both evaluate HN domain structure and conservation (C53-C61). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with crystal structure, NMR comparison, bioinformatics, and CD spectroscopy. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting structural findings and conservation predictions without specific critique.

OpenEval R1 covers crystal structure, SEC-MALLS, and conservation (C6-C52 including C46-C52). Peer R2 evaluates only crystal structure aspects (C46-C52). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledged structure provides important insight but requested additional work on biological significance.

OpenEval R1 includes SEC-MALLS homodimer data (C42-C45) among broader claims. Peer R1 specifically evaluates SEC-MALLS data (C42-C45). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted the data without raising concerns about homodimeric behavior.

Both evaluate heterotetramer formation (C88). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting discrepancy between theoretical and experimental MW but unclear architecture between two possible models. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, specifically questioning generality: 'Is heterotetramerization also applicable to Commd10-Commd2 complex?'

OpenEval R16 evaluates Pur-α structural similarity and DNA/RNA binding speculation (C126-C136 including C131, C135). Peer R11 includes these claims (C131, C135) in broader structural homology critique. OpenEval finds background SUPPORTED but speculation appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN, stating homology analysis is distractive.

OpenEval evaluates major conclusions integrating multiple lines of evidence (C12-C13, C113) about COMM domain dimerization and interactions. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though these conclusions are implicitly addressed through evaluation of component data.

OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C1-C5, C14-C22, C37, C117) establishing biological context and prior knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically critique background claims.
